key_insight: In a young-onset neuropsychiatry cohort, Alzheimer’s and psychiatric polygenic scores showed distinct disease associations, with no detected associations with measured plasma biomarkers.
clinical_relevance: Genetic risk scores may capture information distinct from plasma biomarkers, but their added diagnostic value remains unproven.
method: Studied 687 European-ancestry participants: 195 controls, 283 with primary psychiatric disorders, 55 with Alzheimer’s disease and 154 with other neurodegenerative diseases.
Computed five polygenic risk scores excluding APOE; adjusted models for age, sex and APOE ε4 dose.
Assessed plasma NfL, GFAP and p-tau217 in a 332-participant subset.
evidence_signal: Alzheimer’s and psychiatric scores were associated with their respective diagnoses versus controls (OR per SD: 1.69 and 1.29); adding the Alzheimer’s score to NfL did not improve psychiatric-versus-other-neurodegenerative discrimination meaningfully (AUC 0.764 to 0.773).
watch_item: European-ancestry sampling and limited biomarker availability constrain generalizability; diagnostic utility requires larger, longitudinal validation.
paper_title: Alzheimers disease and psychiatric polygenic risk are disease-specific and independent of plasma biomarkers in a real-world young-onset dementia cohort.
